2609.21663.title: Rethinking Human-Aligned Evaluation: An Analysis of Semantic Metrics Beyond WER
2609.21663.paper_summary: Word Error Rate (WER), the most commonly used metric for Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR), treats every lexical deviation from the reference as equally costly, regardless of whether it changes meaning. This raises the question: does WER actually track how humans judge ASR transcript quality? We introduce HATS-en, an English dataset for human-centered ASR evaluation. Using this dataset, we benchmark lexical metrics against several configurations of BERTScore and SemDist, varying the language model, layer, and pooling strategy. We find that WER agrees least with human judgment among all metrics tested, that the best-performing SemDist configurations achieve the highest overall agreement, ahead of CER and BERTScore, and that no single model is best across settings. CER, despite its simplicity and low cost, remains remarkably close to these best configurations. In line with prior recommendations, our results support shifting ASR evaluation toward CER both for English and for morphosyllabic writing systems as it is a more interpretable and low-cost metric for what evaluation should actually capture, and using SemDist as a complementary evaluation.
2609.21663.paper_summary_zh: 詞錯誤率（WER），是自動語音識別（ASR）中最常用的指標，將每一個與參考文本的詞彙偏差視為同等代價，無論其是否改變了意義。這引發了問題：WER 是否真的能反映人類如何評價 ASR 轉錄質量？我們介紹 HATS-en，一個以人為中心的英語 ASR 評估數據集。使用這個數據集，我們對幾個 BERTScore 和 SemDist 的配置進行了詞彙指標的基準測試，變更語言模型、層和池化策略。我們發現，在所有測試的指標中，WER 與人類判斷的協議度最低，表現最佳的 SemDist 配置達到最高的整體一致性，超過 CER 和 BERTScore，並且沒有單一模型在所有設置中表現最佳。儘管 CER 簡單且成本低，但它仍然與這些最佳配置非常接近。根據先前的建議，我們的結果支持將 ASR 評估轉向 CER，無論是對於英語還是形態音節書寫系統，因為它是一個更具可解釋性和低成本的指標，能夠更好地捕捉評估應該實際涵蓋的內容，並且使用 SemDist 作為補充評估。
